title: Chapter 1 Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of HTML basics, document structure, and best practices!

questions.question: What does HTML stand for?
questions.explanation: HTML stands for HyperText Markup Language. It’s the standard language for creating web pages.

questions.question: Which tag defines the visible content of a webpage?
questions.explanation: The <body> element contains all content that is displayed in the browser window.

questions.question: CSS is responsible for the structure of a web page.
questions.explanation: CSS handles styling and layout; HTML provides the structure.

questions.question: Where does the <title> tag belong?
options: At the very end of the document
questions.explanation: The <title> is metadata and belongs in the <head> section; it sets the browser tab text.

questions.question: What is the correct file extension for a webpage?
questions.explanation: HTML files must use the .html extension to be recognized by web browsers.

questions.question: You need an internet connection to view an HTML file saved on your computer.
questions.explanation: You can open local HTML files directly in a browser without being online.

questions.question: Which tag is used for the main heading of a page?
questions.explanation: <h1> is the highest-level heading and should be used for the main title.

questions.question: How many heading levels does HTML provide?
questions.explanation: HTML defines six heading levels, from <h1> to <h6>.

questions.question: What does <!DOCTYPE html> do?
options: Tells the browser the document type is HTML5
questions.explanation: The doctype declaration instructs the browser to render the page in standards mode using HTML5 rules.

questions.question: HTML comments are written between <!-- and _____.
questions.explanation: An HTML comment starts with <!-- and ends with -->.

questions.question: Comments can be seen by anyone who views the page source.
questions.explanation: HTML comments are part of the source code and visible when viewing the source.

questions.question: Which HTML tag wraps all the other tags?
questions.explanation: The <html> element is the root element that contains the entire HTML document.

questions.question: What attribute should you add to the <html> tag for better accessibility?
questions.explanation: Adding lang="en" (or appropriate language) helps screen readers and search engines.

questions.question: The <head> section is displayed on the page.
questions.explanation: Content in <head> is meta‑information and not rendered in the browser window.

questions.question: Which meta tag is commonly used to set the character encoding to UTF-8?
questions.explanation: The correct syntax is <meta charset="UTF-8">, placed inside <head>.

questions.question: What is the purpose of indentation in HTML?
options: It makes the page load faster
It adds extra spaces on the page
questions.explanation: Indentation doesn’t affect the displayed page but helps developers read and maintain code.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an HTML tag?
questions.explanation: <css> is not a valid HTML tag. CSS is a separate language, not an HTML element.

questions.question: You should have only one <h1> per page for good SEO.
questions.explanation: Best practice is to use a single <h1> to clearly define the page’s main topic.

questions.question: What is the correct way to add a comment in HTML?
questions.explanation: HTML comments use <!-- and --> delimiters.
